canonical_ties.canonical_statement: Let P:D->{0,1}, D subset {0,1}^n, mu a distribution on D, L a nonnegative integer. Suppose every deterministic algorithm making at most L queries computes P under mu with success probability <=beta. If U_1,...,U_r are iid mu, every classical algorithm making at most L queries to each U_h, possibly randomized, adaptive among the r inputs, and given arbitrary additional information independent of (U_1,...,U_r), outputs (P(U_1),...,P(U_r)) with probability <=beta^r.
canonical_ties.note: Deterministic adaptive trees with per-instance caps; no coins or side information.

    (T : S → OutTree (Fin r × κ) (Fin r → Bool)) (hT : ∀ s, (T s).capped fun _ => L) :

theorem classical_prefix_iff {β : Type}
    (T : OutTree (Fin r × κ) β) (τ : ClassicalTranscript r κ)
    (U : Fin r → BitInput κ) :
    classicalPrefix T τ U ↔
      classicalSchedule T τ ∧ ∀ h, classicalLocalConsistent τ h (U h)

premises: Finite independent nonnegative prior weights for the probabilistic interpretation; the equality itself allows arbitrary real weights.
The conditioning transcript has strictly positive total mass.
